# 2026.10.27-01 — Approximations & limitations documentation

## Summary
Documented the physical approximations and usage limitations of PHISE, based on a review of the source code (Context, Target, Companion, Telescope, Interferometer, Camera, SuperKN, N4x4_* architectures, transmission maps, calibration, ROC / test statistics).

## Files modified
- `README.md`: added a project description (mentioning the PhD thesis origin), a "What PHISE can do" list, a "Model scope" table (supported / planned / out of scope) and a link to the documentation.
- `docs/index.md`: mentioned the thesis origin in the introduction, replaced the generic Overview list with the "What PHISE can do" list, replaced the former "Features" section with the "Model Scope" table, and added a "Modelling Details" section (scene, photon flux, geometry/injection, atmosphere/time, chips, detector) before "Quick Links".
- Both files: stated the two core modelling choices (scalar approximation, complex transfer matrices for photonic components) before the scope table.
- Both files: added "Development notes" (hand-written code vs AI-generated documentation, Unicode identifiers and how to type them, absence of independent review).

## Code changes
None.

## Validation
- Sphinx build of `docs/` succeeds; the new sections and inline math render on the index page.
- Polychromatic noise limitation checked numerically (VLTI example context, near-zero flux, `e = 1 s`, `Δλ = 100 nm`): output std ≈ 14 e⁻ in monochromatic mode (√(RON² + dc·e) ≈ 14.1) vs ≈ 683 e⁻ in polychromatic mode with 5 spectral samples.
